mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility is declining week-on-week (11.3% → 7.1%), indicating people are spending less time at home and more time outside. This sustained outbound shift from residential anchors retail-and-recreation mobility upward over the next four weeks as displaced home time converts to discretionary visits.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 4.2 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase relative to the last 28 days, or RESIDENTIAL continues to decline below 5% in the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility has improved consistently (−20.3% → −14.6%), signaling return-to-office momentum. Workers with restored commute routines exhibit higher propensity for retail stops during and after work hours, driving RETAIL_REC upward over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 5.7 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility reverses and falls below −18% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase in the subsequent four-week period.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility has contracted sharply and consistently (−32.1% → −27.9%), indicating suppressed outdoor recreation. When parks remain depressed below −25%, substitution effects redirect discretionary time to indoor retail venues, elevating RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below −25% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at −27.9% in t-0w, consistently below −30% for three weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rebounds above −20% within the next week, or RETAIL_REC does not increase in the subsequent two-week period.

mechanism_narrative: Transit station mobility has improved steadily (−24.6% → −20.3%), indicating restored commute and mobility infrastructure use. Higher transit access enables retail visits; the interaction of rising transit with stable grocery demand signals discretionary retail is recovering alongside essential mobility.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 4.3 points, GROCERY_PHARM improved 0.9 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls below −22% or GROCERY_PHARM falls below −12% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-September in Sydney marks early spring with improving weather. The observed convergence of all mobility indices toward baseline (RETAIL_REC −20.1%, TRANSIT −20.3%, WORKPLACES −14.6%) signals seasonal normalization. Continued weather improvement will push RETAIL_REC further toward baseline over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:All major indices converging toward baseline in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase toward baseline over the next four weeks, or a major weather disruption or policy shock occurs that reverses the convergence trend.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility has stabilized at −10.1%, indicating essential services are accessible and demand is met. When essential mobility is stable and non-threatening, consumer confidence in public spaces rises, enabling discretionary retail to recover. RETAIL_REC will increase over four weeks as confidence effects propagate.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains between −12% and −8% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stabilized at −10.1% in t-0w after three weeks of −11% to −12%
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below −13% or rises above −5% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The gap between WORKPLACES (−14.6%) and RETAIL_REC (−20.1%) has widened to 5.5 points, indicating workers are commuting but not shopping. This gap signals pent-up retail demand among the employed population. Over the next two weeks, this gap will close as workers convert commute trips into retail stops.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES exceeds RETAIL_REC by more than 4 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at −14.6%, RETAIL_REC at −20.1%, gap of 5.5 points in t-0w
failure_condition: The gap between WORKPLACES and RETAIL_REC does not narrow within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC falls further below WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility decline (11.3% → 7.1%) combined with workplace recovery (−20.3% → −14.6%) indicates a shift from home-based to work-based activity. This reallocation of time away from residential anchors, coupled with restored workplace presence, creates a two-week window for retail recovery as commuters and workers engage in discretionary shopping.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 8% AND WORKPLACES improves above −16%
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 7.1%, WORKPLACES at −14.6% in t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 10% or WORKPLACES deteriorates below −17% in the next week, or RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks.
